units.translation: 1138. ἐδεύετο: he was in need, he desired, he demanded. Or because the time of day was lacking. Lm (P)
1145. ἀβολήσομεν: we shall meet. LgP
1150. περιπλομένας: passing by, since a voyage is also called a journey. Callimachus (fr. 278 Schn. = 64, 14 Kapp) 'rouse also someone who has a circuitous voyage'. LmP
7 sch. Nic. Ther. 295 Hesych. πλοῦς Συν. πλοΐζει (344, 3 Ba. Phot. Suid.)
8 ἔγρευ Schneider καί τιν’ ἔχοντα in L : ἔχον τόν in P
1151. μεταχρονίη: as if the mind were not driving. Lm (P)
1156. περὶ παισίν: instead of 'on behalf of the children'. LgP
11 P adds at the end: similar to 'περὶ ξανθῷ Μενελάῳ' (K 240)
1157. παλιντροπίῃσιν: either by the turnings back, or because her soul had been turned back; and she, having fallen into perplexity at the turning back.
1159. σφέλαϊ: the footstool of the throne. LgGgSm(P)
15 τοῦ θρ. in LP : omitted in GS
1161. 〈ὑγρά:〉 instead of 'full of tears'. Lm
1169. οἰόθεν οἶος ἑταίρων: 'alone from among companions' does not fit here; for it means 'alone from many'. But it should have been said 'alone from others'.
17 sch. AB Η 39 Apoll. Lex. Hom. 119, 6 B. Hesych. οἰόθεν οἶος Συν. οἰ. οἰ. (314, 9 Ba. Phot. Suid.) Et. M. 618, 44
17 L as above, P thus: properly it signifies 'alone (Schaefer, -ως PV) from alone'. Homer (Η 226): 'νῦν μὲν δὴ σάφα εἴσεαι οἰόθεν οἶος'. But here it is used instead of 'alone from others'.
1171. κνέφας ἔργαθε νυκτός: periphrastically; the night kept them away. Lg (P)

1172. εὔκηλοι μέλλοντο 〈περὶ σφίσιν〉: a solecism. For the sense is: they were at ease concerning themselves, as if no others were a care to them. But it should have been said 'ἐμέλοντο σφέων', that is, 'of themselves'.
21 μέλλοντο in L : ἐμέλοντο in P
22 ἐμέλοντο — μελόντων — ἐμέλοντο in K : -λλ- supplied by K; άλλων Hoelzlin : ἀλλήλων in L : omitted in P
1177-87a. Ἀονίοιο δράκ〈οντος〉: instead of 'Boeotian'; for Aonia was formerly Boeotia. And Ogygian Thebes from Ogygus, who
24 Et. Gen. (AB) Ἀονία:
24 on the scholia abef cf. W 112; Ἀὼν πόλις Βοιωτίας Sm

ruled over them. Corinna (fr. 31 B. III 551) says that Ogygus was the son of Boeotus. From him also the gates of Thebes. Concerning Europa and the arrival of Cadmus in Thebes, Lysimachus in the first book of his Theban Paradoxes (fr. 4 M. III 336) has collected much conflicting material.

is called Boeotia. ... Apollonius III 1178. Ogygian Thebes from Ogygus, an ancient king (Apollonius etc. in A, omitted in B). sch. Pind. Isthm. VIII 37 c sch. Lyc. 1206 Paus. IX 5, 1 Συν. Ὠγύγιον (420, 23 Ba. Phot. Suid.) Et. M. 820, 37
